name: Plumbing General Skills
audience: People who are new to plumbing and want an entry-level skill
General workers and handymen who work with water systems on site
Maintenance teams that want a broader practical skills base
Anyone considering a career path into formal plumbing qualifications

faqs.q: How much does the Plumbing General Skills course cost?
faqs.a: Pricing depends on group size and delivery mode, so the best way to get an exact quote is to message us on WhatsApp at 061 580 7967. The course runs as daily classes with no waiting period, so you can start as soon as you book. Prices are negotiable for group bookings, and we can deliver at your premises if you have a group to train.

faqs.q: How long does the course take?
faqs.a: The full programme runs over 4 to 6 weeks and combines theory with hands-on practical training. The theory phase takes 8 days and covers plumbing principles, tools, materials, and reading basic diagrams. After that you move into practical work. Daily classes mean you do not have to wait for a set intake date before you start.

faqs.q: Do I need experience before I can do this course?
faqs.a: No. This is an entry-level programme at NQF Level 2, designed for people with little or no plumbing background. You start with plumbing principles, tools, and basic legislation, then build up to installing and maintaining fittings like toilets, basins, and showers. If you already work in maintenance, the course also works as a refresher and skills top-up.

faqs.q: Can you train at our site in Johannesburg or Durban?
faqs.a: Yes. We offer on-site training at client premises, plus centre-based classes in Midrand and Durban. The Midrand centre is at 14 Douglas Road, Glen Austin, and the Durban centre is at 62 Lilian Ngoyi Street, Windermere. For group bookings, on-site delivery is often the most practical option. Call 010 746 6954 or WhatsApp 061 580 7967 to arrange it.

name: Plumbing Safety & Legal Compliance
description: This course covers the health and safety rules that apply to plumbing work in South Africa. It explains the duties of employers and employees under the OHS Act, the basics of COIDA, and how to work safely with tools, pressure systems, excavations, and hot water installations. Learners come away knowing how to identify hazards, follow safe work procedures, and keep the paperwork that proves the work was done properly.
outcomes: Explain the health and safety legislation that applies to plumbing work in South Africa
Identify common hazards on plumbing sites and apply safe work procedures
Understand the duties of employers and employees under the OHS Act
Explain the basics of COIDA and how it applies to workers on site
Work safely with tools, pressure systems, and excavations, and document the work correctly
audience: Plumbers and plumbing apprentices who need a safety foundation
Maintenance staff and handymen who work with water systems
Site supervisors who manage plumbing teams
Contractors who must show clients that their teams work to legal requirements

faqs.q: What safety legislation does this course cover?
faqs.a: The course covers the health and safety rules that apply to plumbing work, including the OHS Act and the basics of COIDA. It looks at the duties of employers and employees, hazard identification, and safe work procedures for tools, pressure systems, and excavations. Certificates are issued in line with SAQA-aligned unit standards where applicable.

faqs.q: Do I need to be a qualified plumber to attend?
faqs.a: No. The course suits anyone who works with or around plumbing systems, including apprentices, maintenance staff, handymen, and site supervisors. If you manage a plumbing team, the course helps you make sure your people work safely and understand their legal duties. New plumbers benefit too, because it builds the safety habits that should be in place from day one.

faqs.q: How much does the course cost?
faqs.a: Pricing depends on group size and delivery mode, so we quote per booking. Message us on WhatsApp at 061 580 7967 with the number of delegates and your location, and we will come back with a price. Daily classes run with no waiting period, and prices are negotiable for group bookings.

faqs.q: Can you present this course at our workplace?
faqs.a: Yes. We deliver on-site at client premises, online, and at our centres. If you have a group of staff, on-site training is usually the most convenient option because there is no travel time. Our centres are in Midrand at 14 Douglas Road, Glen Austin, and in Durban at 62 Lilian Ngoyi Street, Windermere. Call 010 746 6954 or WhatsApp 061 580 7967 to book.

name: Cold Water Plumbing Systems
audience: Plumbers installing or maintaining cold water supply lines
Maintenance technicians who service water systems in buildings
Contractors who need a SAQA-aligned unit standard certificate for their teams
Anyone working toward formal plumbing qualifications

faqs.q: How much does the Cold Water Plumbing Systems course cost?
faqs.a: The course costs R6,000 per delegate and runs over 4 days. Training happens in daily classes with no waiting period, so you can start as soon as you book. Prices are negotiable for group bookings, and we can run the training at your premises if you have a team to train. WhatsApp 061 580 7967 for a group quote.

faqs.q: What certificate do I get?
faqs.a: You receive a certificate issued in line with the SAQA-aligned unit standard 244507, Install, maintain and test cold water supply systems, at NQF Level 4. The certificate shows that you have completed training and can install, test, and maintain cold water supply systems to the standard described in the unit standard.

faqs.q: Do I need experience to do this course?
faqs.a: Some plumbing background helps, because this is an NQF Level 4 programme that moves through installation, testing, and commissioning. If you are new to plumbing, it is better to start with an entry-level course and come back to this one once you have hands-on experience. If you are unsure, message us on WhatsApp and we can advise.

faqs.q: What does the course cover?
faqs.a: The course covers the principles of cold water supply systems, pipe sizing, material selection, valves, fittings, meters, and backflow prevention. You will practise installing systems, testing pressure, finding faults, and doing routine maintenance. It also covers interpreting drawings and the documentation and handover procedures that clients expect. System isolation and shutdown procedures are covered as well, so you know how to work on a system safely.

name: Hot Water Systems (Geysers & Boilers)
audience: Plumbers who install or service geysers and hot water pipework
Maintenance teams responsible for hot water systems in buildings
Contractors working on renovations and new installations
Technicians who want a SAQA-aligned unit standard for hot water systems

faqs.q: How much does the Hot Water Systems course cost?
faqs.a: The course costs R6,000 per delegate and runs over 5 days. Training happens in daily classes with no waiting period, so you can start as soon as you book. Group bookings are negotiable, and we can deliver on-site at your premises. WhatsApp 061 580 7967 to book or to ask for a group price.

faqs.q: What does the course cover?
faqs.a: The course covers hot water supply systems, including geysers and boilers, from principles and system types through to installation, testing, and commissioning. You will work with pipework, fittings, insulation, pressure control, and temperature regulation, and learn fault finding and routine servicing. It also covers shutdown and isolation procedures and the documentation needed for handover.

faqs.q: Do I need to be qualified before I do this course?
faqs.a: This is an NQF Level 4 programme, so some plumbing experience is expected. You should be comfortable with basic plumbing work before you start, because the course moves quickly through installation and testing of hot water systems. If you are new to plumbing, start with a general skills course first. Not sure where you fit? WhatsApp us and we will point you in the right direction.

faqs.q: What certificate will I receive?
faqs.a: You receive a certificate issued in line with the SAQA-aligned unit standard 244496, Install, maintain and test hot water supply systems, at NQF Level 4. It shows that you have completed training in installing, maintaining, and testing hot water supply systems. For booking details, call 010 746 6954 or WhatsApp 061 580 7967.

name: Drainage & Rainwater Systems Installation
audience: Plumbers and drain layers working on below-ground drainage
Construction teams installing stormwater and rainwater systems
Maintenance contractors who service drainage and gutter systems
Contractors who need accredited certificates for their site teams

faqs.q: How much does the Drainage & Rainwater course cost?
faqs.a: The course costs R6,000 per delegate and runs over 5 days. It covers two unit standards: 244498, Install, maintain and test below ground drainage systems, and 244495, Install, maintain and test rainwater systems. Daily classes run with no waiting period, and group bookings are negotiable. WhatsApp 061 580 7967 for a quote.

faqs.q: Is this course accredited?
faqs.a: Yes. It is an accredited plumbing skills course at NQF Level 4, covering two SAQA unit standards, one for below-ground drainage systems and one for rainwater systems. Certificates are issued in line with these unit standards. You can book by calling 010 746 6954 or emailing info@rehtraining.co.za. Group bookings can be arranged at your premises, and prices are negotiable.

faqs.q: What will I be able to do after the course?
faqs.a: After the course you will be able to install, test, and maintain below-ground drainage systems and rainwater systems. That includes excavation and trenching, pipe laying with correct gradients and jointing, inspection chambers and gullies, gutters and downpipes, and testing and commissioning. The practical focus means you leave ready to apply it on site.

faqs.q: Can you train at our site?
faqs.a: Yes. We offer on-site training at client premises, online, and centre-based classes. Our centres are in Midrand, 14 Douglas Road, Glen Austin, and Durban, 62 Lilian Ngoyi Street, Windermere. For a construction team, on-site delivery saves travel time and lets you train around your schedule. Contact us on 010 746 6954 or WhatsApp 061 580 7967.

faqs.q: What certificate do I get?

It confirms that you have completed training in installing and maintaining solar water heating systems. For bookings, call 010 746 6954 or email info@rehtraining.co.za. name: Pipe Laying & Jointing
audience: Construction workers and pipe layers on civil projects
Site teams installing stormwater and underground pipelines
General workers moving into specialised pipe laying roles
Contractors who need accredited civil construction certificates

faqs.q: How much does the Pipe Laying & Jointing course cost?
faqs.a: The course costs R6,000 per delegate and runs over 5 days. It is an accredited civil construction skills course covering unit standard 12903, Install storm water pipelines, at NQF Level 2. Daily classes run with no waiting period, and group prices are negotiable. WhatsApp 061 580 7967 to book, or email info@rehtraining.co.za if you prefer to book in writing.

faqs.q: Do I need experience to do this course?
faqs.a: No, this course is set at NQF Level 2, so it suits workers who are new to pipe laying as well as those already on construction sites. You will learn to interpret drawings, prepare excavation sites, install stormwater pipes, and use the correct jointing methods for concrete, steel, and plastic pipes. If you already work on site, it formalises the skills you use daily.

faqs.q: What will I learn on the course?
faqs.a: The course covers stormwater and underground pipeline systems, reading construction drawings, excavation techniques, trenching safety, and ground support. You will practise jointing concrete, steel, and plastic pipes, test pipelines for alignment and leaks, and learn backfilling and compaction methods. It also covers culverts, manholes, site housekeeping, and environmental considerations. Safety on the trench is a running theme through the practical work.

faqs.q: Can you train at our site in Johannesburg or Durban?
faqs.a: Yes. We deliver on-site at client premises, online, and at our centres in Midrand and Durban. For construction teams, on-site training is usually the best fit because you can train where the work happens. Call 010 746 6954 or WhatsApp 061 580 7967 to arrange a date, and we will quote for your group.

Maintenance technicians who deal with leaks, blockages, and pressure problems
Property and facilities managers who maintain water systems
Contractors who need specialised plumbing repair skills on their teams

faqs.a: The course costs R6,000 per delegate and runs over 5 days. It covers unit standard 244494, Perform specialised fault-finding and repairs to plumbing systems, at NQF Level 4. Daily classes run with no waiting period, and group bookings are negotiable. WhatsApp 061 580 7967 for a quote or to book.

faqs.q: What does the course cover?
faqs.a: The course covers systematic fault-finding on hot and cold water systems, drainage, and waste systems. It also covers replacement of worn components, recommissioning, and preventive maintenance strategies.

faqs.q: Who should attend this course?
faqs.a: The course suits plumbers and maintenance technicians who already have plumbing basics and want to specialise in fault-finding and repairs. It is also useful for property managers who oversee water systems. Because it is an NQF Level 4 programme, some hands-on plumbing experience is expected. Not sure if it fits? Message us on WhatsApp 061 580 7967 and we will advise.

faqs.q: Where is the training held?
faqs.a: Training is available at our centres in Midrand, 14 Douglas Road, Glen Austin, and Durban, 62 Lilian Ngoyi Street, Windermere, or on-site at your premises for group bookings.
